findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_my_comments" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.detail: Description of "publish_post" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never, mandatory). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp-server" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_posts, get_post_analytics, list_my_comments, list_leads, attach_images, repurpose_post, schedule_post, publish_post · Private data: list_my_comments, list_leads, attach_images, schedule_post, publish_post · Public sink: list_posts, get_post_analytics, write_post_in_my_voice, attach_images, repurpose_post, generate_ideas, schedule_post, publish_post.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_posts, get_post_analytics, list_my_comments, list_leads, attach_images, repurpose_post, schedule_post, publish_post · Private data: list_my_comments, list_leads, attach_images, schedule_post, publish_post · Public sink: list_posts, get_post_analytics, write_post_in_my_voice, attach_images, repurpose_post, generate_ideas, schedule_post, publish_post

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
